creativeDirection: Daylight location photography of a real winter street corner, using the band portrait as the only cast and translating the graphic sleeves into weather, small physical objects, and light phenomena within one plausible scene.
scene: A cold winter street corner outside an old brick corner shop beside a frozen canal or snow-covered basin, with slushy pavement, bare masonry, and a broad pale sky reflected in the shop windows.

elements.element: the four band members stand together against the real brick wall of the corner shop, keeping their original row arrangement and styling
the location is a corner shop on a city pavement, seen from a slightly wide street angle with receding sidewalk and large windows
snowbanks and a frozen water edge sit just beyond the shop, and a small black-and-white dog sits near the lower right foreground facing the camera
the three colorful emblems become three small real objects suspended on thin wires above the street: a tiger-head shop ornament, a burst-shaped paper decoration, and a six-pointed star light
a faint shooting-star form appears as a real curved neon tube reflection or hanging light arc above and behind the group, subtle and physical rather than graphic
a lavender plume of fine vapor or powdery light haze drifts across the cold air near the shopfront, airy and sparse

coverSummaries.album: Meet The Eels Essential Eels Vol 1 1996 2006
coverSummaries.description: A minimalist cover with a worn, yellowed paper background and a vertical golden strip along the left edge like a book spine. Near the top center is a small bouquet of white daisy-like flowers with yellow centers and green stems. The rest of the composition is mostly empty space with centered text elements.
coverSummaries.medium: graphic design with paper texture and small illustration

coverSummaries.description: A mostly monochrome snowy landscape with a frozen or still body of water in the foreground and snow-covered banks receding into the distance. In the lower right sits a small black-and-white dog facing the camera. Across the top are three separate colorful illustrated emblems spaced horizontally: a roaring tiger head, an exploding firecracker or cannon-like object with a burst, and a six-pointed star emblem with a blue center.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: three colorful symbols floating above a snowy landscape

coverSummaries.description: A dark, grainy, green-tinted image resembling a night photograph or distressed print. In the center-lower area is a black outlined shooting star or comet shape with a star at one end and several curved trailing lines extending to the right. The edges are vignetted and rough, with dark structural forms framing the sides.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: outlined shooting star with trailing arcs

coverSummaries.description: An abstract image on a pale gray-white background. From the left-center spreads a soft purple cloud or blur that transitions into fine looping lines, wispy filaments, and scattered spiky dots drifting toward the right. The composition is airy and sparse, with the abstract form concentrated across the middle.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: purple cloud of wispy lines and spiky particles

coverSummaries.description: A black-and-white band portrait against a brick wall, with a large red handwritten-style graphic across the upper portion. Four young adults stand in a row wearing dark clothing. From left to right: one person with shaggy dark hair facing forward, one person with a dark bob haircut turned in profile, one person with short light hair facing forward with hands clasped, and one person with short dark hair looking slightly to the side. The image is high-contrast and grainy.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: four band members standing against a brick wall
coverSummaries.medium: black-and-white photograph with overlaid graphic text
coverSummaries.people: four young adults standing against a brick wall

coverSummaries.description: A high-contrast black-and-white street photograph taken with a wide-angle or fisheye effect. A corner shop with large windows dominates the right side, while a tiled sidewalk and street recede into the distance on the left. A lone person in a light coat walks away along the pavement. Blue block text spans the top of the cover.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: fisheye view of a corner shop on a city street
coverSummaries.medium: black-and-white photograph with overlaid graphic text
coverSummaries.people: one person walking away on the sidewalk

prompt: A real winter street corner beside a frozen canal, seen from street level in a three-quarter view, with an old brick corner shop and broad pale sky reflected in large windows; the four people from reference image 5 are the primary subject, standing together against the actual brick wall in the same row, pose, gaze, hair, and styling as their cover portrait, sharply visible and recognisable. Include the corner-shop architecture and receding pavement from reference image 6, but no other cast people. Near the lower right foreground, the small black-and-white dog from reference image 2 sits facing the camera on snowy slush. Above the street, translate the three colorful symbols from reference image 2 into small real hanging objects on thin wires: a tiger-head ornament, a burst-shaped paper decoration, and a six-pointed star light. Translate the shooting-star motif from reference image 3 into a subtle physical curved neon or tube-light reflection arcing in the air above and behind the group. Let reference image 4 appear as a sparse lavender vapor plume drifting lightly across the cold air near the shopfront. Add the tiny bouquet of white daisies from reference image 1 tucked into a doorway ledge or wall crack, with aged cream-and-yellow paper tones in trim and notices. Photographic realism, crisp daylight location photography, clean detail, no posters or murals, no album art reproduced on surfaces. Frame it as one cohesive moment with the band off-centre and the shop and frozen edge layered around them, bright overcast winter daylight, high clarity, cool air, restrained saturated accents against brick, snow, and gray sky. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 5 shows four young adults standing against a brick wall, and reference image 7 is an enlarged close-up of those same people - take their faces from reference image 7. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference image 6 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, and do not get round that by copying a sleeve flat onto a mural, banner, poster, billboard, tapestry, wall panel, screen, or floor graphic; transform their non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image brightly and cleanly: open, readable shadows and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere.
